## LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN — profile (page 116)

- Header facts: 21 countries; Population 587 million; GNI 6,051; unit line: US$ billion, unless otherwise indicated.

- Total external debt stock 2025: 2,219.
- Change from 2024: +9.3%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25:
  - Printed start value (2015): 1,601.
  - Printed end value (2025): 2,219.
  - Line shape: overall rising trend from 2015 to 2025; increases through the late 2010s, is roughly flat around ≈2020–21, rises again through ≈2023, is about flat at ≈2023–24, then jumps to the series peak in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 2,219.
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 1,149.
  - Private nonguaranteed: 807.
  - Short-term: 264.

  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 350.
    - Bilateral: 37.
    - Private creditors: 761.

  - Multilateral:
    - IDB: 97.
    - World Bank-IBRD: 80.
    - Other multilateral: 174.

  - Bilateral:
    - China: 11.
    - France: 10.
    - Other bilateral: 16.

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 133%, +2.8%; line fluctuates, peaks around the middle of the period, then declines and edges down to 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 37%, +4.7%; line rises to a mid-period peak, then falls and is broadly flat to slightly up by 2025.
  - Debt service / exports: 22%, -4.7%; line rises early, remains volatile, dips late in the period, then partially rebounds before ending slightly lower in 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 6%, -2.9%; line is volatile, rises to a late-period high, drops sharply, then recovers somewhat by 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 20 yrs.
    - Grace period: 5 yrs.
    - Interest rate: 5.4%.
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: 14 yrs.
    - Grace period: 8 yrs.
    - Interest rate: 6.0%.

- Notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of Latin America and the Caribbean DRS reporting countries.
- Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
